title: President Trump's Cyber Strategy for America
summary: The 2026 cyber strategy organizes federal action under six policy pillars and calls for sustained coordination across government, industry, academia, allies, offensive and defensive operations, critical services, supply chains, and modernized information systems. Security is presented as a foundation for innovation and economic continuity.
key_findings: The strategy calls for coordinated government and private-sector action at greater speed and scale.
Critical infrastructure, supply chains, federal systems, and essential services are explicit protection priorities.
Modernization, resilience, disruption of adversaries, and international standards are connected.
why_it_matters: It frames cybersecurity as an operating condition for infrastructure, manufacturing, finance, and emerging technology rather than a separate digital topic.
ftfn_relevance: Supports cyber backlinks across energy, water, supply chains, compute, and government systems.
Creates implementation questions around shared services, modernization, standards, and recovery.
evidence_limits: A national strategy does not demonstrate that networks or infrastructure operators have implemented the stated controls.
Some offensive and intelligence activity is necessarily outside the public record.
